title: Implement cmd/wc word, line, and byte counter (prd005-wc R1-R6)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd005-wc.yaml (all requirements for the wc implementation)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (module github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils, file layout conventions)
  - go.mod (Go version and module path)

files:
  - path: cmd/wc/main.go
    action: create
    note: "wc implementation -- flag parsing, counting logic, multi-file output, error handling"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: >
      Implement flag parsing and counting per prd005-wc R1 and R2. Default mode (no flags)
      counts lines, words, and bytes. -l counts newline characters; -w counts maximal
      sequences of non-whitespace per unicode.IsSpace; -c counts bytes; -m counts Unicode
      rune count (each invalid UTF-8 byte counts as one character); -L reports the longest
      line length with tabs expanded to the next multiple of 8. When flags are combined,
      emit counts in fixed column order regardless of flag order: lines, words,
      chars-or-bytes, max-line-length per prd005-wc R2.6. -m overrides -c when both
      are specified per prd005-wc R2.3.
  - id: R2
    text: >
      Implement multi-file output with dynamic column alignment and totals per prd005-wc R3.
      Collect all per-file counts first, then right-align each count column to the width of
      the largest value in that column across all files per prd005-wc R3.1. Print a "total"
      line with the arithmetic sum of all counts when multiple files are given per
      prd005-wc R3.2. Support --total=auto (default), --total=always, --total=only, and
      --total=never per prd005-wc R3.3.
  - id: R3
    text: >
      Implement special input handling per prd005-wc R4 and R5. Treat "-" as a filename
      argument meaning stdin per prd005-wc R4.1. Handle binary input without corruption or
      panic per prd005-wc R4.2. Handle zero-byte input producing all-zero counts per
      prd005-wc R4.3. Support --files0-from=FILE to read NUL-delimited filenames from FILE;
      when FILE is "-", read filenames from stdin per prd005-wc R4.4. Under LC_ALL=C,
      -m and -c produce identical counts per prd005-wc R5.
  - id: R4
    text: >
      Implement exit codes per prd005-wc R6. Exit 0 when all inputs are processed
      successfully. Exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened or read -- print an error
      message to stderr for each failed file and continue processing remaining files before
      exiting 1 per prd005-wc R6.2. Exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout per
      prd005-wc R6.3.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: >
      cmd/wc is a main package. The single source file is cmd/wc/main.go per the project
      convention that each cmd/ package contains main.go as the implementation file.
      No external dependencies beyond the Go standard library are required.
  - id: D2
    text: >
      Multi-file output requires a two-pass approach: collect counts for all files in the
      first pass to determine the maximum count values and thus column widths, then format
      and print in the second pass per prd005-wc R3.1.
  - id: D3
    text: >
      Word splitting uses unicode.IsSpace per prd005-wc R2.2 -- a word is a maximal
      sequence of runes for which unicode.IsSpace returns false.

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: >
      printf 'foo\nbar baz\n' | ./bin/wc produces output whose whitespace-delimited
      fields are "2", "3", and "12" in that order, matching gwc on the same input.
  - id: AC2
    text: >
      ./bin/wc on two files produces per-file count lines and a "total" line with
      right-aligned integer columns matching gwc output byte-for-byte under LC_ALL=C.
  - id: AC3
    text: >
      ./bin/wc given a non-existent file argument prints a diagnostic to stderr, exits
      with code 1, and still processes and reports counts for any accessible files on
      the command line.
  - id: AC4
    text: >
      go build ./cmd/wc/... and golangci-lint both complete with no errors or warnings.

title: Implement cmd/du recursive disk usage (prd009-du R1, R2, R3, R4+R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd009-du.yaml
  - pkg/sys/fileinfo.go (FileInfo struct -- Blocks, Dev, Ino, Size fields)
  - pkg/sys/signal.go (InstallSIGPIPEHandler function signature)
  - pkg/format/humansize.go (HumanSize function and HumanSizeOpts type)
  - cmd/wc/main.go (manual flag parsing pattern to follow)

files:
  - path: cmd/du/main.go
    action: create
    note: complete du utility -- flag parsing, recursive traversal, deduplication, output

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: |
      Implement recursive directory traversal per prd009-du R1: use os.ReadDir to
      iterate directory entries; call pkg/sys.Lstat on each entry to obtain st_blocks
      (FileInfo.Blocks, in 512-byte units); accumulate 1024-byte block counts
      (Blocks / 2) per directory and print one "SIZE\tPATH\n" line per directory with
      the cumulative total; default to "." when no arguments are given; process
      multiple arguments independently in command-line order; do not follow symlinks
      during traversal (use Lstat, not Stat).
  - id: R2
    text: |
      Implement all flag behaviors per prd009-du R2 using manual flag parsing matching
      the cmd/wc/main.go pattern -- no flag package: -h displays sizes as
      human-readable strings via pkg/format.HumanSize with binary mode (1024-based,
      HumanSizeOpts{}); -s prints only one line per argument (total only, no
      subdirectory lines, equivalent to --max-depth=0); -a prints one size line per
      file and directory; -d N limits reported depth (entries deeper than N are
      accumulated into parent but not printed as separate lines); -k accepts 1024-byte
      blocks without error (the default); -m reports sizes in 1048576-byte blocks
      (Blocks / 2 / 1024, rounded up to 1 minimum); -c appends a grand total line
      "SIZE\ttotal\n" after all arguments; --apparent-size uses os.FileInfo.Size()
      instead of FileInfo.Blocks.
  - id: R3
    text: |
      Implement hard-link deduplication per prd009-du R3: maintain a
      map[uint64]map[uint64]bool keyed by (Dev, Ino) across the entire invocation;
      obtain Dev and Ino from pkg/sys.Lstat (FileInfo.Dev and FileInfo.Ino); when a
      (Dev, Ino) pair has already been counted, add zero blocks for that entry;
      deduplication applies across all arguments, not per argument.
  - id: R4
    text: |
      Implement exit codes and signal handling per prd009-du R4 and R5: call
      pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler at startup so piping to head exits silently; exit
      0 when all arguments traverse successfully; exit 1 when any traversal error
      occurs -- print a diagnostic to stderr ("du: PATH: ERROR") for each error,
      continue processing remaining entries and arguments, then exit 1 after all
      processing completes.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: |
      Use os.ReadDir for directory iteration rather than filepath.Walk to control
      pkg/sys.Lstat calls explicitly; DirEntry.Info() does not return extended
      metadata (st_blocks, st_dev, st_ino), so call pkg/sys.Lstat separately on each
      entry path.
  - id: D2
    text: |
      Accumulate block counts bottom-up: recurse into a subdirectory first, obtain
      its cumulative block total, then add that total to the parent accumulator. A
      directory's reported block count is the sum of all contained files and
      subdirectories including itself.
  - id: D3
    text: |
      For -d N depth limiting, pass the current depth as an int parameter in the
      recursive traversal function; print a size line for an entry only when its
      depth is <= N; always accumulate its blocks into the parent regardless of
      whether it is printed.
  - id: D4
    text: |
      Parse flags manually by iterating os.Args[1:]; handle combined short flags
      (e.g., -sk, -ak), the -- end-of-flags sentinel, and --apparent-size as a long
      option. Accept -d N as two separate tokens or --max-depth=N as one token.

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: |
      go build ./cmd/du compiles without errors; the binary produces "SIZE\tPATH\n"
      output for "du -k ." in a non-empty directory and exits 0.
  - id: AC2
    text: |
      Hard-link deduplication is correct -- two directory entries pointing to the same
      (Dev, Ino) inode contribute blocks only once to the reported total.
  - id: AC3
    text: |
      -s produces one line per argument (no subdirectory lines); -h produces
      human-readable suffixes via pkg/format.HumanSize; -c appends a "SIZE\ttotal\n"
      line; -a includes a line for every file encountered; -d 1 limits output to the
      argument and its immediate children.
  - id: AC4
    text: |
      When given a non-existent path, the binary prints a diagnostic to stderr, exits
      1, and still processes any remaining valid arguments. golangci-lint reports no
      warnings on cmd/du/main.go.

title: GH-29: Recurring: Full generation run — clean end-to-end with minimal context
description:
This is the sixth generation run. Previous runs established the pipeline works but each had a disqualifying flaw:

- eng04 (run 1): succeeded but predates current scaffold version; no releases filter; seeded incrementally
- eng07 (run 2): 32k output token limit blocked stitch agents
- eng08 (run 3): 295K prompt → 10m46s first-turn latency → 15m timeout before code was written
- eng09 (run 4): measure validation retry loops (3×3 invocations) produced 0 LOC
- eng10 (run 5): seeded from v1 tags — gave the agent 2842+1744 LOC head start, defeating the benchmark

This run must be clean: start from specs-only (0 Go LOC), let measure propose everything from scratch.

Goals:
1. Demonstrate cobbler-scaffold can go from specs-only to passing differential tests end-to-end.
2. Determine the correct multi-release generation strategy (single vs. sequential generations).
3. Establish a principled, minimal context configuration.

title: Implement cmd/cat concatenate utility (prd006-cat R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd006-cat.yaml (all flag behaviors, transformation order, exit codes)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (cmd/ package structure and conventions)
  - go.mod (module path github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils)

files:
  - path: cmd/cat/main.go
    action: create
    note: cat utility -- passthrough, line numbering, blank squeezing, non-printing display, error handling

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default behavior: read named files in order, or stdin when no files are given or '-' is given as a filename; write contents verbatim to stdout; handle binary input (all byte values 0x00-0xFF) without corruption; do not add or remove newlines from the input (prd006-cat R1.1-R1.5)"
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement line-numbering flags -n and -b: -n prepends a right-justified 6-wide line number followed by a tab character to every output line using format '%6d\\t'; -b prepends a number only to non-blank lines, leaving blank lines without a number or tab; -b overrides -n when both are given; a blank line is defined as a line containing only a newline character (prd006-cat R2.1-R2.4)"
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement blank-line squeezing -s: collapse two or more consecutive blank output lines to one; the first blank line is written and subsequent consecutive blank lines are discarded; squeezing applies across file boundaries when multiple files are concatenated; apply squeezing before line numbering so suppressed blank lines do not consume line numbers (prd006-cat R3.1-R3.3)"
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement non-printing display flags -v, -E, -T, -A, -e, -t, -u: -v encodes control characters 0x00-0x1F (except tab 0x09 and newline 0x0A) as ^X where X is 64 positions higher, 0x7F as ^?, and bytes 0x80-0xFF with M- prefix; -E appends '$' before each newline; -T displays tab as '^I'; -A equals -v -E -T combined; -e equals -v -E; -t equals -v -T; -u accepted without effect; apply transformations in order: squeeze blanks, non-printing display, end-of-line marker, line-number prefix (prd006-cat R4.1-R4.9)"
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement error handling and exit codes: exit 0 on success; exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened -- print error message to stderr and continue processing remaining file arguments; exit 1 on stdout write error; do not exit non-zero due to SIGPIPE when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer (prd006-cat R5.1-R5.4)"

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Module path is github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils per go.mod; binary entry point is cmd/cat/main.go with package main; no external dependencies beyond the Go standard library"
  - id: D2
    text: "Apply transformations in the fixed order from prd006-cat R4.9: squeeze blanks (-s) first, then non-printing display (-v/-T), then end-of-line marker (-E), then line-number prefix (-n/-b); this order is non-negotiable per the spec"
  - id: D3
    text: "Read input line-by-line using bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\\n') rather than bufio.Scanner, so that partial last lines (no trailing newline) are preserved without reconstruction; the newline byte (when present) is included in the returned slice and must be preserved in output"
  - id: D4
    text: "Handle SIGPIPE by catching syscall.SIGPIPE via os/signal and calling os.Exit(0) so that piping cat output to head or other truncating consumers exits cleanly without a broken-pipe error message, matching gcat behavior (prd006-cat R5.4)"

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "'go build ./cmd/cat/' succeeds with no errors and produces a runnable binary"
  - id: AC2
    text: "Default mode: all 256 byte values (0x00-0xFF) pass through without corruption when no flags are active; output bytes are identical to input bytes"
  - id: AC3
    text: "-n produces format '     N\\t' (6-wide right-justified number followed by tab) for every output line including blank lines; -b produces the same format for non-blank lines only, blank lines receive no number and no tab; -b takes precedence over -n when both are given"
  - id: AC4
    text: "-s with input containing four consecutive blank lines produces exactly one blank line in output; squeezing applies across file boundaries so the last blank line of one file and the first blank line of the next file count as consecutive"
  - id: AC5
    text: "-v encodes: 0x01 as '^A', 0x1B as '^[', 0x7F as '^?', 0x80 as 'M-^@', 0xA0 as 'M- ', 0xFF as 'M-^?'; tab (0x09) and newline (0x0A) are not altered by -v"
  - id: AC6
    text: "-A produces output byte-for-byte identical to applying -v, -E, -T simultaneously; -e produces output identical to -v -E; -t produces output identical to -v -T"
  - id: AC7
    text: "A non-existent file argument causes a descriptive error message on stderr and an exit code of 1; any remaining valid file arguments on the command line are still read and written to stdout before the process exits"

title: Implement pkg/testutils differential testing harness (prd001 R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/testutils component section)
  - go.mod (module path for import declarations)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest.go
    action: create
    note: DiffTest struct, NormalizeFunc type, RunDiffTests entry point, binary execution, comparison and reporting, file-state comparison
  - path: pkg/testutils/normalizer.go
    action: create
    note: TimestampNormalizer built-in normalizer

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Define the DiffTest struct per prd001 R1.1-R1.4 with fields Args []string, Stdin []byte, Env []string, ExitCode int, Normalizers []NormalizeFunc, FileExpectations []FileExpectation, and WDir string. Define NormalizeFunc as func([]byte) []byte. Define FileExpectation as a struct with Path string and Content []byte. Nil Stdin means immediate EOF; nil Env means the binary inherits the test process environment; nil or empty Normalizers means no normalization is applied."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement binary execution per prd001 R2.1-R2.5: RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) invokes both binaries with identical Args, Stdin, and Env, captures stdout/stderr/exit code from each independently, imposes a 10-second default timeout (fail with clear timeout message if exceeded), and uses a per-test os.MkdirTemp working directory when DiffTest.WDir is empty."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement comparison and reporting per prd001 R3.1-R3.6: apply DiffTest.Normalizers in order to both binaries' stdout and stderr before comparison; compare normalized stdout byte-for-byte, normalized stderr byte-for-byte, and exit codes exactly; report divergence with triggering args, stdin truncated to 256 bytes, both stdouts, both stderrs, and both exit codes; run each DiffTest as a t.Run named subtest using the DiffTest index or a name derived from its args."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement normalization composition per prd001 R4.1-R4.3: the Normalizers slice on DiffTest is applied left-to-right to both binaries' outputs before comparison. Implement TimestampNormalizer in normalizer.go as a NormalizeFunc that replaces strings matching the ts default strftime format '%b %d %H:%M:%S' (e.g. 'Feb 19 14:05:32') with the fixed placeholder 'TIMESTAMP' using a compiled regexp."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement file-state comparison per prd001 R5.1-R5.2: after both binaries exit, for each FileExpectation in DiffTest.FileExpectations read the file at Path (relative to the test working directory used by that binary's invocation) and compare its content byte-for-byte with FileExpectation.Content, reporting path and both file contents on divergence using the same t.Errorf format as stdout divergence."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Name the primary file difftest.go because the primary exported type is DiffTest, per the project file naming convention (testutils/testutils.go is forbidden)."
  - id: D2
    text: "RunDiffTests signature is RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) per prd001 AC1. The function is the sole public entry point for the harness."
  - id: D3
    text: "The Normalizers field on DiffTest is []NormalizeFunc (a slice, not a single function) per prd001 R4.3. Both binaries' outputs are passed through the same normalizer sequence before byte-for-byte comparison."
  - id: D4
    text: "Use exec.CommandContext with context.WithTimeout for binary invocation per prd001 R2.3. Set the default timeout to 10 seconds via a package-level constant DefaultTimeout = 10 * time.Second. Do not expose a per-test timeout override in this task."
  - id: D5
    text: "Each binary invocation runs in its own subdirectory under the per-test temp directory so that file-state comparisons (prd001 R5) read files written by the correct binary without cross-contamination."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "A caller can define []DiffTest and invoke RunDiffTests(t, goBinaryPath, refBinaryPath, tests) with no other setup, per prd001 AC1."
  - id: AC2
    text: "A passing DiffTest run emits no test output. A failing run prints the triggering args, stdin (truncated to 256 bytes), and both binaries' stdout, stderr, and exit code, per prd001 AC2."
  - id: AC3
    text: "TimestampNormalizer replaces a string matching the ts default format (e.g. 'Feb 19 14:05:32') with 'TIMESTAMP' so that ts differential tests pass despite wall-clock differences, per prd001 AC3."
  - id: AC4
    text: "A DiffTest with a FileExpectation whose expected content differs from what one binary writes causes a test failure reporting the path and both file contents, per prd001 AC4."
  - id: AC5
    text: "A DiffTest whose binary exceeds 10 seconds fails immediately with a clear timeout message and does not hang the test run, per prd001 AC5."
  - id: AC6
    text: "go build ./pkg/testutils/... succeeds and golangci-lint reports no warnings on pkg/testutils/, per prd001 AC6."

title: Implement cmd/ts timestamp utility (prd004-ts R1-R8)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (cmd/ component, project structure)
  - go.mod (module path: github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils)

files:
  - path: cmd/ts/main.go
    action: create
    note: ts binary -- read stdin line by line and prepend strftime timestamps

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default behavior (prd004-ts R1.1-R1.6): read stdin line by line with bufio.NewReader ReadString, prepend a timestamp formatted with '%b %d %H:%M:%S' and a space before each line, flush stdout after every line, pass through partial last lines without trailing newline, and exit 0 on clean EOF."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement custom format string (prd004-ts R2.1-R2.4): accept an optional positional argument as a strftime format string; translate standard strftime directives to Go time.Format layout strings; implement ts-specific subsecond extensions %.S (seconds.microseconds), %.s (unix-epoch.microseconds), %.T (HH:MM:SS.microseconds) by formatting the base component then appending '.' and six decimal digits from a single time.Now() call per line."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement incremental mode (prd004-ts R3.1-R3.4): -i flag timestamps each line with elapsed time since the previous line (first line uses elapsed since start); default format '%H:%M:%S' with UTC for elapsed formatting; -i and -s are mutually exclusive -- print usage error to stderr and exit non-zero if both are given."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement elapsed-since-start mode (prd004-ts R4.1-R4.3): -s flag timestamps each line with total elapsed time since ts started, monotonically increasing; default format '%H:%M:%S' with UTC for elapsed formatting; overridden by a custom format argument."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement monotonic clock mode (prd004-ts R5.1-R5.3): -m flag selects time.Now() monotonic reading for all timestamp samples; compatible with all format modes including subsecond extensions; timestamps must not jump backwards."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement relative-time conversion mode (prd004-ts R6.1-R6.5): -r flag scans each line for recognized timestamp patterns -- syslog ('Jan  5 14:30:00'), ISO-8601 ('2024-01-05T14:30:00.000Z'), RFC 2822 with optional day, lastlog ('Mon Jan  5 14:30') -- and replaces each match with a relative age string (e.g., '15m5s ago'); if a custom format argument is also given, reformat matched timestamps via that strftime format instead; lines without a recognized timestamp pass through unchanged; -r is mutually exclusive with -i and -s."
  - id: R7
    text: "Implement exit codes and error handling (prd004-ts R7.1-R7.3): exit 0 on clean stdin EOF; exit non-zero and print a usage message to stderr for unrecognized flags; handle SIGPIPE by installing a signal handler that calls os.Exit(0) when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer, suppressing broken-pipe errors."
  - id: R8
    text: "Implement TZ environment handling (prd004-ts R8.1-R8.2): honor the TZ environment variable for wall-clock timestamps in default mode by loading the time.Location from the TZ value before formatting; use UTC internally for elapsed timestamp formatting in -i and -s modes regardless of the process TZ setting, matching the TZ=GMT behavior of the Perl source."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Use time.Now() for all clock reads. Go's time.Time automatically carries a monotonic reading, so -m mode requires no special clock selection -- the same call satisfies both wall-clock and monotonic requirements (prd004-ts R5.1)."
  - id: D2
    text: "Implement strftime by translating standard directives (%Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, %b, %j, %p, %Z, %%, etc.) to Go time.Format layout strings before calling Format(). For the three ts subsecond extensions (%.S, %.s, %.T), extract the base component via Format(), then append '.' and fmt.Sprintf('%06d', t.Nanosecond()/1000) for microsecond precision (prd004-ts R2.3)."
  - id: D3
    text: "For -i and -s elapsed timestamps, compute the duration, convert to whole seconds (int64), and call time.Unix(seconds, 0).UTC().Format(layout) to produce the HH:MM:SS string under UTC semantics, matching the TZ=GMT behavior of the Perl source (prd004-ts R3.2, R4.2)."
  - id: D4
    text: "Use bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin) with ReadString('\\n') to read lines. This correctly handles partial last lines (no trailing newline at EOF) and avoids bufio.Scanner's 64 KB default buffer limit (prd004-ts R1.5)."
  - id: D5
    text: "For -r mode, compile the four timestamp regexes once at startup with regexp.MustCompile. Compute relative age as time.Since(parsedTime) and format as '<Xh><Ym><Zs> ago' with only non-zero components shown, except always show seconds (prd004-ts R6.1-R6.2)."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "echo 'hello world' | go run ./cmd/ts produces a line matching '<month> <day> <HH:MM:SS> hello world' using the default '%b %d %H:%M:%S' format (prd004-ts AC1)."
  - id: AC2
    text: "printf 'a\\nb\\nc\\n' | go run ./cmd/ts -s produces three lines with monotonically non-decreasing elapsed timestamps in HH:MM:SS format (prd004-ts AC2)."
  - id: AC3
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts -z (unrecognized flag) prints a usage message to stderr and exits with a non-zero code (prd004-ts AC4)."
  - id: AC4
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts with empty stdin (immediate EOF) produces no output and exits 0 (prd004-ts AC5)."
  - id: AC5
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts -i -s prints a usage error to stderr and exits non-zero (prd004-ts R3.4)."
  - id: AC6
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts -r on input 'Jan  1 00:00:00 boot message' outputs a line where the syslog timestamp is replaced by a relative age string followed by the remaining content (prd004-ts R6.1-R6.2)."
  - id: AC7
    text: "cmd/ts compiles successfully with go build ./cmd/ts/... and produces no warnings under golangci-lint (prd004-ts AC6)."

title: cmd/du differential tests -- prd009-du R1-R5 (test-rel02.0 du section)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - cmd/du/main.go (existing du implementation -- flags, output format, exit codes)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel02.0.yaml (du test cases, fixtures, and preconditions)

files:
  - path: cmd/du/du_test.go
    action: create
    note: differential tests for cmd/du covering all test-rel02.0.yaml du test cases

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: |
      Implement TestMain that builds the Go du binary into a temp directory via
      "go build -o <tmpdir>/du ." and locates the Homebrew GNU reference binary
      via exec.LookPath("gdu"). Set package-level vars goBinary and refBinary;
      leave goBinary empty on build failure so downstream tests skip gracefully.
      Clean up the temp directory with os.RemoveAll in a deferred call before
      os.Exit(code). Per prd009-du acceptance criteria AC9.
  - id: R2
    text: |
      Implement makeDuFixture(t *testing.T) that creates a temp directory tree:
      root/subdir1/file_a.txt (1024 zero bytes, 0644), root/subdir2/file_b.txt
      (2048 zero bytes, 0644), and root/root_file.txt (512 zero bytes, 0644).
      Returns the fixture root path. Used by du_default_recursive, du_summary_mode,
      du_all_files, du_human_readable, du_max_depth_1, du_kilobyte_units,
      du_megabyte_units, and du_apparent_size test cases.
  - id: R3
    text: |
      Implement TestDuDifferential that defines a []testutils.DiffTest slice and
      calls testutils.RunDiffTests(t, goBinary, refBinary, tests). The slice must
      include all 11 du test cases from test-rel02.0.yaml: du_default_recursive
      (args: ["-k", fixtureDir]), du_summary_mode (["-sk", fixtureDir]),
      du_all_files (["-ak", fixtureDir]), du_human_readable (["-h", fixtureDir]),
      du_max_depth_1 (["-k", "-d", "1", fixtureDir]), du_grand_total
      (["-ck", subdir1, subdir2]), du_apparent_size (["--apparent-size", "-k",
      fixtureDir]), du_kilobyte_units (["-k", fixtureDir]), du_megabyte_units
      (["-m", fixtureDir]), and du_missing_path (["-k", "nonexistent_dir"]).
      All entries use Env: []string{"LC_ALL=C"} and nil Normalize.
  - id: R4
    text: |
      For du_hard_link_dedup: create a separate fixture using t.TempDir() containing
      dir_a/shared.txt (regular file with 1024 zero bytes) and dir_b/shared.txt
      created via os.Link(dir_a/shared.txt, dir_b/shared.txt) so both entries share
      the same inode. Run with args ["-k", hardlinkRoot]. The test confirms the
      differential comparison passes -- both gdu and the Go binary count the
      shared inode only once. Per prd009-du R3.1-R3.3.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: |
      Follow the exact pattern from cmd/cat/cat_test.go: package main, goBinary and
      refBinary as package-level string vars set only in TestMain, baseEnv as
      []string{"LC_ALL=C"}, all fixtures created via t.TempDir() in the test
      function body. Do not use testdata/ subdirectories or committed fixture files.
  - id: D2
    text: |
      No normalization functions are needed for any du test case. Per
      test-rel02.0.yaml preconditions, du output is deterministic when both binaries
      stat the same files on the same filesystem. Set Normalize: nil on all DiffTest

title: GH-31: Rewrite all PRDs to be self-contained and atomically scoped
description:
The current PRDs have two structural problems that cause stitch agent failures:

**Problem 2: Requirements grouped by flag family, not by implementation unit.**

title: Rewrite prd008-ls R1-R2: embed syscall API and split long format into atomic requirements
description:
Split prd008-ls R2 (long format) into 5 atomic requirements and embed all external API signatures inline. R2 currently bundles three independent subsystems (permission formatting, owner/group resolution, mtime formatting) into one requirement, causing stitch task timeouts.

## Files to Modify

## Requirements

### R1 changes
In R1.1, embed function signatures inline and remove "(prd002-sys R1.1)" and cross-references to prd003-format:
- TerminalWidth: func TerminalWidth() (int, error) from pkg/sys — returns current terminal column count via TIOCGWINSZ ioctl on stdout; returns error when stdout is not a terminal.
- Columns: func Columns(entries []string, termWidth int) [][]string from pkg/format — distributes entries into the maximum number of columns fitting within termWidth, sorted vertically (down then across).

### R2 split — replace single R2 with 5 requirements

**R2a: -l flag skeleton and permission string**
-l must produce long format. Field order (left to right): permissions (10 chars), nlink, owner, group, size, mtime, name. Fields separated by a single space. Numeric fields (nlink, size) are right-aligned.
Permission string algorithm (10 characters):
- Position 0 (file type): 'd'=directory, 'l'=symlink, 'c'=char device, 'b'=block device, 'p'=FIFO, 's'=socket, '-'=regular file. Derived from fi.Mode.
- Positions 1-3 (owner rwx): r/- for bit 0o400, w/- for 0o200, x/- for 0o100. If setuid (0o4000) is set: replace x with 's' if execute set, 'S' if not.
- Positions 4-6 (group rwx): bits 0o040, 0o020, 0o010. If setgid (0o2000) is set: replace x with 's' or 'S'.
- Positions 7-9 (other rwx): bits 0o004, 0o002, 0o001. If sticky (0o1000) is set: replace x with 't' or 'T'.

**R2b: Nlink, size, and pkg/sys.FileInfo**
Long format must obtain file metadata via pkg/sys.Lstat(path string) (*sys.FileInfo, error).
FileInfo struct (embed inline): Mode os.FileMode; Size int64; Nlink uint64; Uid uint32; Gid uint32; Rdev uint64; Dev uint64; Ino uint64; Blocks int64 (512-byte blocks); Blksize int64; ModTime time.Time.
- Nlink: fi.Nlink uint64 — right-align in column wide enough for all entries.
- Size (bytes): fi.Size int64 — right-align in column wide enough for all entries. With -h, replaced by HumanSize output (see R5).

**R2c: Owner and group name resolution**
Resolve owner name: call os/user.LookupId(strconv.Itoa(int(fi.Uid))); on success use u.Username; on error use strconv.FormatUint(uint64(fi.Uid), 10).
Resolve group name: call os/user.LookupGroupId(strconv.Itoa(int(fi.Gid))); on success use g.Name; on error use strconv.FormatUint(uint64(fi.Gid), 10).
Fields are left-aligned (pad with spaces to column width across all entries).

**R2d: Modification time formatting**
Format fi.ModTime (time.Time from pkg/sys.FileInfo):
- If time.Since(fi.ModTime) < 6*30*24*time.Hour: use fi.ModTime.Format("Jan _2 15:04")
- Otherwise: use fi.ModTime.Format("Jan _2  2006")
Both formats produce a 12-character field. Right-align in column.

**R2e: Total block count line and symlink display**
Before directory listing print "total N\n" where N = sum of fi.Blocks for all listed entries, divided by 2 (converts 512-byte blocks to 1K blocks). N is a plain integer.
Symlink display: if fi.Mode & os.ModeSymlink != 0, read target via os.Readlink(path); append " -> " + target to the name field. Use Lstat (not Stat) so the symlink's own metadata is used.

## Acceptance Criteria
- R2 is replaced by R2a through R2e in prd008-ls.yaml

- FileInfo struct with Go types is embedded inline in R2b

## Requirements

### R4 changes (color output)
In R4.3, replace "(prd003-format R2.1-R2.4)" with an inline ANSI color table and reset value. No pkg/format call is required — the stitch agent implements color lookup directly in cmd/ls:

File type → ANSI escape sequence:
- directory:         "\033[34m"   (blue)
- symlink:           "\033[36m"   (cyan)
- executable file:   "\033[32m"   (green)
- block device:      "\033[33;1m" (yellow bold)
- character device:  "\033[33;1m" (yellow bold)
- socket:            "\033[35m"   (magenta)
- named pipe (FIFO): "\033[33m"   (yellow)
- regular file:      ""           (no color)
Reset sequence: "\033[0m"

Each entry name is wrapped as: colorCode + name + resetCode. When color is suppressed, both codes are empty strings.
Executable detection: mode & 0o111 != 0 (any execute bit set).

### R5 changes (human-readable sizes)
In R5.1 and R5.2, replace "(prd003-format R3.1-R3.4)" with inline HumanSize binary algorithm:

HumanSize binary algorithm (1024-based):
- If bytes == 0, return "0"
- Suffixes: []string{"", "K", "M", "G", "T", "P", "E"}
- Divide bytes by 1024 repeatedly until < 1024, counting suffix index
- If bytes % 1024 == 0 at the chosen unit: format as "%dSuffix" (e.g., "4K")
- If remainder != 0: format as "%.1fSuffix" (e.g., "1.5K")
- Apply to fi.Size int64 for file size column in -l output

R5.2: Apply same algorithm to the "total N" block count (N = sum(fi.Blocks)/2 as int64, then HumanSize). Output as "total X" where X is the human-readable string.

### R7 changes (signal handling)
In R7.1, replace "(prd002-sys R3.1-R3.2)" with inline handler pattern:
Install SIGPIPE handler at startup: use signal.Notify with a buffered channel; in a goroutine, call os.Exit(0) when the channel receives. Do not use signal.Ignore. No pkg/sys import needed.

In R7.2, replace "(prd002-sys R4.1-R4.2)" with inline SIGWINCH pattern:
Install SIGWINCH handler at startup: use signal.Notify with a buffered channel; in a goroutine, re-query terminal width via pkg/sys.TerminalWidth() and update the column layout width. pkg/sys.TerminalWidth() signature: func TerminalWidth() (int, error) — import pkg/sys for this call only.

title: Implement cmd/sponge soak-before-write utility (prd007-sponge R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd007-sponge.yaml
  - go.mod (module path github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils and Go version)

files:
  - path: cmd/sponge/main.go
    action: create
    note: sponge utility implementation -- soak all stdin before writing to output file

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: |
      Implement the core soak-before-write contract (prd007-sponge R1): buffer stdin
      in memory using a dynamically grown byte slice starting at 8192 bytes and
      doubling on overflow; when the buffer reaches or exceeds 1 MiB (1048576 bytes),
      spill the current buffer to a temp file created via os.CreateTemp in the
      directory from TMPDIR env var (falling back to os.TempDir()) with prefix
      "sponge", then continue reading stdin into the temp file; open the output file
      only after stdin returns io.EOF. Register a signal handler (SIGINT, SIGTERM,
      SIGHUP, SIGPIPE) via os/signal that deletes the temp file and calls os.Exit(1)
      before the rename completes.
  - id: R2
    text: |
      Implement output file handling (prd007-sponge R2): when an output filename is
      given, attempt os.Rename of the temp file to the output path; on rename failure
      (cross-device or other error), fall back to byte-for-byte copy of temp file
      content to the output file, then delete the temp file. Before writing, call
      os.Lstat (not os.Stat) on the output path; if it exists and is a regular file,
      read its Mode() and apply it to the output file via os.Chmod after writing. When
      the output file does not exist, use default mode 0666 masked by the process umask.
      The output file must never be in a partially-written state observable by other
      processes.
  - id: R3
    text: |
      Implement append mode (-a, prd007-sponge R3) and passthrough mode (prd007-sponge R4):
      in append mode, open the existing output file and copy its content into the temp
      file first, then append the buffered stdin content; when the output file does not
      exist in append mode, behave identically to default mode. In passthrough mode (no
      output filename argument), if a temp-file spill occurred, seek the temp file to
      offset 0 and copy its content to os.Stdout; if no spill occurred (buffer fits in
      memory), write the in-memory buffer directly to os.Stdout without creating a temp
      file.
  - id: R4
    text: |
      Implement error handling and exit codes (prd007-sponge R5): exit 0 on success;
      exit 1 and print a descriptive message to stderr via fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ...)
      on any failure -- stdin read error, temp file create or write failure, output file
      open failure, rename failure, or copy failure. Delete the temp file in all exit
      paths via defer so it never persists after the process exits, whether due to
      success, error, or signal.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: |
      Temp file creation: os.CreateTemp(tmpdir, "sponge") where tmpdir is
      os.Getenv("TMPDIR") falling back to os.TempDir(). Store the temp file path
      immediately and register a defer to os.Remove it. This satisfies prd007-sponge
      R1.4 and R5.4.
  - id: D2
    text: |
      Memory threshold: use a fixed 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) constant as the spill
      threshold. When the accumulated buffer length reaches this threshold, write
      everything to the temp file and set a spilled=true flag. Subsequent reads go
      directly to the temp file via io.Copy from the remaining stdin.
  - id: D3
    text: |
      Flag parsing: use the standard flag package. Register -a as a bool flag.
      Accept zero or one positional argument after flag.Parse() as the output
      filename. Print usage to os.Stderr and call os.Exit(1) on unrecognized flags
      or more than one positional argument.

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: |
      "printf 'hello' | ./bin/sponge" writes "hello" to stdout and exits 0,
      verifying passthrough mode with in-memory buffer (no temp file created because
      input is under the 1 MiB threshold).
  - id: AC2
    text: |
      The soak-before-write contract holds: create data.txt with known content, run
      "cat data.txt | ./bin/sponge data.txt", confirm the resulting data.txt contains
      the original content unchanged, proving the output file was not opened before
      stdin was fully consumed.
  - id: AC3
    text: |
      "printf 'appended\n' | ./bin/sponge -a existing.txt" where existing.txt contains
      "original\n" produces a file containing "original\nappended\n", verifying append
      mode copies the original content before the stdin content.
  - id: AC4
    text: |
      When sponge overwrites an output file whose mode is 0640, the resulting file
      retains mode 0640 after the write, verifying permission preservation via lstat
      and chmod.
  - id: AC5
    text: |
      "mage build" produces ./bin/sponge and cmd/sponge compiles with no warnings
      under golangci-lint.
